subject: Re: Parallel Pathway — rate limit & concurrency handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Parallel Pathway — post-demo recap and concurrency clarifications

Hi Hannah — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right handoff for your infra/finance team.

Key notes from the call:
- Primary SLO: user-facing chat generation p95 target of ~400ms (token streaming enabled).
- Streaming: partial tokens streamed to client; soft chunk latency target <200ms for first token, steady per-chunk latency goal <150ms.
- Typical request durations: 2–8s when streaming; median ~3s.
- Integration pattern: you indicated the front-end will multiplex requests over a small pool of long-lived connections (keepalives).

Questions for Atlass:
1) Peak concurrent in-flight requests we should plan for (not sockets) — you mentioned “spikes during morning sync” but can you give a rough number?
2) Do you expect requests to be evenly distributed across regions or concentrated in us-east?
3) Will you multiplex many independent user sessions over a handful of sockets, or will each client open several sockets? Any rough expected connection count?

What we propose next (our side):
- We’ll prepare a short rate-limit / connection policy (reserved concurrency + burst buffer + socket guidance) tailored to your traffic pattern.
- If you can share a 24–72h traffic sample (timestamps + request ids + payload size) that would let us recommend an ideal reserved concurrency level and connection-pool sizing.

Action items / timeline:
- Hannah to share traffic sample (CSV) and confirm peak concurrent in-flight requests.
- Redwood (Jordan + Marissa) to send a draft rate-limit + connection policy within 48 hours.

Attachment: placeholder for traffic sample (please send CSV export).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
Office: +1 415-555-0182

From: Hannah Cole <hannah.cole@atlashealth.com>

Cc: Akira Sato <akira.sato@atlas.health>, Atlas Health - Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Parallel Pathway — post-demo recap and concurrency clarifications

Thanks Jordan — good recap. A few answers below and I attached a lightweight traffic sample (anonymized): atlas-traffic-sample.csv.

Answers:
- Peak concurrent in-flight requests: steady peaks are ~80 concurrent requests for 20–30 minutes during morning digest runs.
- Burst behavior: we see daily short spikes that reach ~300 concurrent in-flight requests for ~5–8 minutes when a system-wide notification batch hits.
- Connections: our web tier multiplexes user sessions onto ~120 long-lived keepalive sockets (we prefer to minimize socket churn).
- Regions: primarily us-east, with a small fraction (~8%) in eu-west for regulatory fallbacks.

Notes / asks:
- How does Redwood enforce burst caps (do you drop, 429 + Retry-After, or queue)? We’d prefer graceful throttling + clear headers so our client can backoff politely.
- We may need an SLA exception for the morning digest window if you recommend a reserved concurrency approach.

Attaching the traffic sample; procurement looped in to start paperwork when we have a proposed capacity/price.

— Hannah
Hannah Cole
Director, Engineering — Atlas Health
hannah.cole@atlashealth.com
[Attachment: atlas-traffic-sample.csv]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Parallel Pathway — rate-limit & concurrency handoff (internal recommendation)

Quick internal note based on Atlas sample and Hannah’s reply:

Summary of Atlas profile:
- Steady peak: ~80 concurrent in-flight
- Short daily bursts: ~300 concurrent for 5–8 minutes
- Connection pool target: ~120 sockets (keepalives)
- Mostly us-east, small eu-west fallback (8%)

Recommendation (for initial proposal):
1) Offer a Dedicated reserved concurrency slab sized to cover steady peak + safety buffer. Recommend reserved concurrency = 160 (2x steady peak) to keep p95 latency under 400ms under normal load.
2) Provide a burst buffer policy (token bucket) for short spikes up to 350 concurrent for up to 10 minutes; beyond that, enforce 429 + Retry-After with explanatory headers.
3) Socket guidance: recommend client pool of 100–150 keepalive sockets. Our runtime will multiplex many in-flight streams per socket; provide example HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 keepalive params.
4) Streaming SLOs: we can meet <200ms first-chunk if reserved concurrency in place; for burst windows, p95 may slip to ~600ms unless burst buffer is active.

Pricing / procurement note:
- Suggest we present this as an add-on to their Hosted plan or as a low-tier Dedicated commitment (quarterly). Ben, can you draft a simple price delta for reserved concurrency 160 + burst buffer? Keep an option for a 6-month commit (discounted).

I’ve attached a draft rate policy to send to Atlas after Ben and Jordan OK the numbers.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-draft-rate-policy.pdf]

1) We’ll send a short formal proposal today that includes: reserved concurrency = 160, burst buffer allowing up to 350 concurrent for 10 minutes, socket guidance (100–150 keepalives), and exact retry behavior (429 + Retry-After + X-Redwood-Quota headers).
2) Ben will include a price delta for Dedicated or an add-on to Hosted with a 6-month commit option.
